thread:
anya: FYI - getting multiple customer reports (cust-phi, cust-b2b) of p95 latency spike for requests originating EU -> US since ~04:20 UTC. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings. Symptoms: TLS handshake latency and extra cross-zone hops. p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~2.2s. Anyone oncall?

sre-bot: [ALERT] edge-egress-latency-eu-us p95=2200ms @ 2026-03-17T04:22:14Z - ticket INC-5432 created.

leo: @anya can you paste a traceroute + a curl timing sample? Which POPs are showing the issue (eu-west vs eu-central)?

anya: quick traceroute from eu-west client -> our egress:
```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.example (54.23.11.9), 30 hops max
 1  eu-pop-01 (10.1.1.1)  5.2 ms  4.9 ms  5.0 ms
 2  transit-ix (34.199.2.2)  12.3 ms  13.1 ms  12.8 ms
 3  us-pop-02 (52.14.77.5)  1250 ms  1248 ms  1255 ms
 4  api.redwood-inference.example (54.23.11.9)  1251 ms  1250 ms  1253 ms
```

curl -w "time_namelookup:%{time_namelookup} time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat
=> time_namelookup:0.012 time_connect:0.030 time_appconnect:2.180 time_total:2.240

This looks like a transatlantic hop taking ~1.2s.

sam: I see matching metrics in our egress histogram: TLS handshake (appconnect) p99 jumped from ~80ms -> ~1.6s. DNS resolution steady. CPU/GPU on hosts normal. Likely a routing/GSLB steering issue causing EU clients to be sent to US POPs.

leo: Possible quick mitigations: 1) bias GSLB to prefer eu-west/central for EU source ASN ranges, 2) apply temporary route affinity to keep sessions local, 3) throttle concurrent handshakes to reduce queueing. I can run a safe dry-run of the route bias.

anya: doing dry-run now:
```
# dry-run output
$ rwctl route-bias apply --src-region=eu --prefer-region=eu-west --weight=100 --dry-run
plan: would shift ~82% of eu traffic to eu-west, no downtime expected
```

anya: applying change at 04:42 UTC now.

anya: applied. quick smoke for one customer (cust-phi): p95 dropped from 2.2s -> 190ms within 2m. still watching for other clients.

support-ops: FYI auth logs: increased connection timeouts during spike caused a bunch of transient 401/504s (timeouts at token fetch), but token validation still looks fine. No billing API failures observed.

sam: adding short-term limiter on concurrent handshakes per source IP to reduce thundering:
```
# ephemeral config
conn.limit.handshakes.per_ip=32  # applied to edge proxy pool
```

leo: I've opened a provider support ticket to investigate a recent GSLB config change that may have shifted weights: SR-9982. Creating follow-up postmortem: PM-678. INC-5432 will be updated.

anya: Good catch. For the incident timeline: 04:20 alerting -> 04:22 spike detected -> 04:30 dry-run -> 04:42 apply -> 04:48 p95 stabilized. Monitoring for 30m before close.

sam: I'll keep collecting TLS handshake histograms and correlate with BGP/Anycast metrics.

leo: Nice work. Once stable, let's rollback the limiter and plan a controlled test to repro with BGP/GSLB changes.

anya: Thanks team :thumbsup: we'll reconvene in 30m for status.

support-ops: Noted. Adding customer comms template to INC-5432.

sre-bot: [RESOLVE] Alert edge-egress-latency-eu-us acknowledged - mitigation applied (route-bias -> eu-west).
